questions.text:
Language [latex]L_{1}[/latex] is polynomial time reducible to language [latex]L_{2}[/latex]. Language [latex]L_{3}[/latex] is polynomial time reducible to [latex]L_{2}[/latex], which in turn is polynomial time reducible to language [latex]L_{4}[/latex]. Which of the following is/are true?
I. if [latex]L_{4} \in P[/latex], then [latex]L_{2} \in P[/latex]
II. if [latex]L_{1} \in P[/latex] or [latex]L_{3} \in P[/latex], then [latex]L_{2} \in P[/latex]
III. [latex]L_{1} \in P[/latex], if and only if [latex]L_{3} \in P[/latex]
IV. if [latex]L_{4} \in P[/latex], then [latex]L_{1} \in P[/latex] and [latex]L_{3} \in P[/latex]
questions.solution:
Reductions: [latex]L_1\le L_2[/latex], [latex]L_3\le L_2\le L_4[/latex]. If the target is in P, the source is in P.

- I: [latex]L_4\in P\Rightarrow L_2\in P[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- IV: then [latex]L_1, L_3\in P[/latex] too [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II and III would need reductions in the other direction [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not implied

Answer: I and IV only

questions.text:
Which of the following languages are context-free?
[latex]L_{1}=\{a^{m}b^{n}a^{n}b^{m}|m,n\geq 1\}[/latex]
[latex]L_{2}=\{a^{m}b^{n}a^{m}b^{n}|m,n\geq 1\}[/latex]
[latex]L_{3}=\{a^{m}b^{n}|m=2n+1\}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1=a^mb^na^nb^m[/latex]: nested matching (outer m, inner n) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] push a's, push b's, pop on a's, pop on b's [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL.
- [latex]L_2=a^mb^na^mb^n[/latex]: crossed matching, which one stack cannot do [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not CFL.
- [latex]L_3=a^{2n+1}b^n[/latex]: push for a's, pop for b's [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL.

Answer: L1 and L3 only

questions.text:
Consider the following policies for preventing deadlock in a system with mutually exclusive resources.
I. Processes should acquire all their resources at the beginning of execution. If any resource is not available, all resources acquired so far are released
II. The resources are numbered uniquely, and processes are allowed to request for resources only in increasing resource numbers
III. The resources are numbered uniquely, and processes are allowed to request for resources only in decreasing resource numbers
IV. The resources are numbered uniquely. A process is allowed to request only for a resource with resource number larger than its currently held resources
Which of the above policies can be used for preventing deadlock?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I removes hold-and-wait (all or nothing).
- II, III and IV each impose a single global order on requests (increasing or decreasing), which removes circular wait.

All four prevent deadlock.

Answer: Any one of I, II, III, and IV

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Any one of I and III but not II or IV
Any one of I, III, and IV but not II
Any one of II and III but not I or IV
Any one of I, II, III, and IV
